deities: Guru Granth Sahib (installed in the sanctum; Sikh worship uses no idols)

history.dynasty: Sikh (Guru Gobind Singh period; present structure 20th century)
history.period: Fort founded 1689; Khalsa founded on Vaisakhi, 30 March 1699; present building raised 1936-1944
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib is one of the five Takhts (temporal seats of authority) of Sikhism and the birthplace of the Khalsa Panth: here on 30 March 1699 Guru Gobind Singh Ji administered khande di pahul (amrit) to the Panj Pyare (Bhai Daya Ram, Bhai Dharam Das, Bhai Himmat Rai, Bhai Mohkam Chand, Bhai Sahib Chand) and then took amrit from them himself. The town was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur as Chak Nanaki (land bought from Rani Champa of Bilaspur on 19 June 1665). Guru Gobind Singh lived here 25 years and built a ring of defensive qilas (Anandgarh, Lohgarh, Holgarh, Fatehgarh, Taragarh) with Kesgarh at the centre; construction began 1689 and took over ten years. The present two-tier complex with fluted lotus dome dates to major 20th-century works (1936-1944); it preserves historic shastars (weapons) of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. NOTE: Wikipedia notes the 1930s structure rose over the original Anandgarh Qila site - verify.

name: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib
town_description: Anandpur Sahib, in Rupnagar district at the Shivalik foothills, is one of Sikhism's holiest cities - the 'City of Bliss' founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur and the birthplace of the Khalsa. Its historic fort-gurdwara complex, the Virasat-e-Khalsa museum, and the annual Hola Mohalla gathering draw devotees worldwide.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, about 80 km away (~90 minutes by taxi); Amritsar's Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport is about 170 km away.
travel.railway: Anandpur Sahib has its own railway station, connected to major cities.
travel.road: On the Guru Gobind Singh Marg (NH 205); well connected by bus/taxi from Chandigarh, Amritsar and Delhi.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May to witness Hola Mohalla and Vaisakhi; October to March for pleasant weather otherwise.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Specific hours unverified; gurdwaras here are typically open from early morning (around 4:00 AM) to late evening (around 10:00 PM) - verify locally.
